_rule: The IAM instrument catalogue (author 2026-10-15: 'Sell me the IAM instrument catalogue'). One source for Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/INSTRUMENTS.md, the README's catalogue table and the page's catalogue section (CANON/catalogue.py). The words are written here; every status line is computed from the Master Testing Manifest rows named, so it cannot fall behind. Voice: we. No hype words.
why_self_reference: Until now every instrument needed a reference: healthy cells of the same kind, often from the same laboratory, to say what normal looks like. That reference is the hardest thing in this field to get, and it is why most tests work in one lab and stumble in the next. Across 56 kinds of healthy human cells, we found that a cell's tagging mistakes follow one straight line set by how loosely it holds its own DNA. So a healthy cell's expected reading can come from its own sample. An instrument that carries its own reference does not need a library of other people's cells, does not inherit another lab's quirks, and can be pointed at any tissue, any lab, even any species that tags its DNA. That step is now commissioned: IAM-A reads each sample against its own reference.
together: Each instrument answers a different question about the same sample, so together they leave no blind side. IAM-Atlas v2.1 is the healthy reference every reading uses. The IAM-Deconvolver says whose DNA it is: which cells are in the sample, and in what shares. Met-A says how far each of those cells has drifted toward the ceiling. The C-Score says whether the pattern has started to clump. IAM-A says whether each mark is still held at its own healthy rate. Group-A says whether a whole group has moved, for studies rather than single patients. Every reading is also drawn on the globe, where it sits on the genome, against its healthy reference. A tumor that hides from one reading still has to answer to the others.

instruments.name: IAM-Atlas v2.1
instruments.question: What does each healthy cell look like, at every site, and how sure are we?
instruments.how: A map of 79 kinds of healthy human cells, built from 21 public sources on arrays and sequencing, fitted as one model so every spot on the genome carries its value and its uncertainty. Like combining many sensors into one estimate, each weighted by how far it can be trusted.
instruments.next: Deposited with its DOIs (fitted atlas 10.5281/zenodo.23441999; posterior draws 10.5281/zenodo.23422688). On the site every cell turns on the Globe Explorer, the noise maps from the posterior draws are drawn, and every report carries the sample on the same globe against its healthy reference. In the works: the information sphere (below, In development) and each cell's change layer on the globe.
instruments.specialty: It is the map every other instrument reads against: for 79 healthy cell types, the expected tagging at every site with its range of error, so a sample can be split into its cells and each cell compared with its own healthy kind.
instruments.commissioned: 79 cell types; met all three sealed bars against both published reference atlases, 2026-10-16; commissioned for three cell references and the colon and lung tissue tests
instruments.what: Its values are on the array scale (its sequencing sources are placed on that scale), and it is the ruler for arrays; sequenced samples read against the IAM Sequencing Atlas, counted from sequencing reads, because an array never quite reads 0 or 1 and sequencing does.

instruments.name: IAM-Deconvolver
instruments.question: How much of each cell is in a mixed sample?
instruments.how: Reads a mixed sample against IAM-Atlas v2.1 and reports each cell's share with its range, after a sample check that refuses arrays it cannot read. On 200 fresh mixtures from a laboratory the atlas never saw, the shares came back within 0.016 of the truth (mean absolute error). Read and flagged development: every one of the atlas's 79 cells in one run; nine known mixtures of tissue DNA in blood were found at the right size through the one command (mean error 0.0057, nothing that was not put in above 0.0030; `doors/data/DEV_ONE_DRAW_01/run_03/mixes_03_summary.txt`).
instruments.commissioned: blood-cell shares on arrays, tested on neutrophils, monocytes, CD4 T and CD8 T cells, 2026-10-17
instruments.next: Commission the B and NK cell shares; then the full 79-cell panel and plasma, both already read and flagged.
instruments.specialty: It turns a whole-blood array into its cells, so each instrument reads the cell it was built for and a change in the mix is not mistaken for a change in the cells.

instruments.name: Met-A
instruments.question: How far has a tissue's tagging level drifted toward the ceiling?
instruments.how: Reads the methylation level at each cell's identity sites, sites a healthy cell holds mostly marked or mostly unmarked, steadily from one healthy sample to the next, chosen away from the ends so that wear can show; against a healthy reference, on cheap and plentiful arrays. Commissioned on isolated neutrophils. Each cell is read at its own identity sites, the sites it holds (where a loss can raise disorder) and healthy people agree on; reading every site is more sensitive but cannot say which cell is losing hold (DEV-EACH-CELL-01 exploration 4). Read and flagged development: Met-A for every cell the IAM-Deconvolver finds, each against its own profile in IAM-Atlas v2.1, on arrays and on sequencing values.
instruments.next: The sealed test of Met-A against the atlas with same-slide references; then every cell in a mix.
instruments.specialty: Cost and reach: a single array, the most common methylation measurement in the world, read on the gauge against the same cell type's healthy reference, with its detection limit printed.
instruments.commissioned: tested and commissioned on isolated neutrophils, EPIC v1, 2026-10-09

instruments.name: C-Score (the clustering meter)
instruments.question: Has the pattern started to clump?
instruments.how: Cancer does not only shift tagging levels; it clumps them into runs. The C-Score measures that clumping against a healthy band. The band held in three laboratories that never helped set it, and one person measured twice reads the same. Reproduced through the one command from the raw arrays: the band holds again.
instruments.next: Real cancers read on the gauge; then 450K, EPIC v2 and plasma; new same-person repeats from a series that did not help build the band. Its family (below, In development): the whole-genome C-Score against the atlas, and IAM-A's.
instruments.commissioned: tested and commissioned on whole blood, EPIC v1, 2026-10-15
instruments.specialty: The shape of a change, not its size: whether a sample's departures from healthy are scattered like ordinary wear or packed together in stretches, the way a tumor that silences or loses a region leaves them. It is the clustering step of the cosmic microwave background analysis chain, carried over to the genome.

instruments.name: IAM-A
instruments.question: Is each mark still held at its own healthy rate?
instruments.how: Counts tagging mistakes one DNA molecule at a time, the most direct reading of informational fidelity we have, and reads them against the sample's own line. The physics end of the catalogue: the floor and ceiling are derived, and since 2026-10-15 the healthy middle comes from the sample itself. Every reading states its own counting error: how many held-error chances it counted and the range that leaves.
instruments.next: Other healthy blood cells, then tissue and cell-free DNA; the tumor pairs read on the gauge; the firm rate derived again on the commissioned counter (the top physics item); the whole-genome IAM-A globe (development).
instruments.specialty: That it reads single molecules and carries its own reference: how well each molecule held its marks, compared with the healthy level set by the cell's own loose share, with no library of other people's cells.
instruments.commissioned: each sample against its own reference; sealed test on healthy blood CD8 T cells, whole-genome bisulfite, 2026-10-17

instruments.name: Group-A
instruments.question: Has a whole group moved (a trial arm, an exposure, a cohort)?
instruments.how: Single blood readings are too noisy for one person on arrays, but a group average is not. Group-A reads each person with the one command, tares each reading against healthy arrays run the same way, and compares the groups. On 278 healthy people from a laboratory it had never read, women and men came out 0.36 % apart, and a 1 % loss planted into half of them was found at 7.253 standard errors.
instruments.next: One cancer at a time, patients and healthy controls from the same series.
instruments.specialty: Groups: whether a whole cohort, trial arm or exposure has moved, read as one, with patients and healthy comparisons run in the same laboratory series.
instruments.commissioned: groups of whole bloods run in one series, EPIC v1, 2026-10-20

support_tools.name: Intake and calibration
support_tools.what: Takes an array's raw intensities, checks every control, and turns them into tagging levels on one fixed scale, refusing what it cannot read and saying why.

support_tools.name: The tare
support_tools.what: Reads each specimen against healthy references run beside it, so a laboratory's own offset cancels instead of passing for disease.

support_tools.name: Composition
support_tools.what: For whole blood, works out which cells are in the sample and in what shares, so a change in the mix is not mistaken for a change in the cells.

support_tools.name: The chain and its report
support_tools.what: Runs every stage in a fixed order, records every input and setting, and prints one report per sample with each instrument's reading, its status and its detection limit.

support_tools.name: The sky sphere and the Globe Explorer
support_tools.what: Lays every site of IAM-Atlas v2.1 on one sphere in genome order, the way a microwave sky is drawn: equal area, no edges, clustered change shows as patches, and the microwave-sky toolset applies. Every report draws the sample on it against its healthy reference; the change is fixed by the measurement (blocks of 10 neighboring sites beyond the 5 % family-wise line), and a slider only fades the unchanged background. The Explorer carries the atlas's 79 cells and the example readings.

chemistry_intro: DNA's sequence is the same in every cell; the methyl tags are not, and a sequencer cannot see a tag directly. So the DNA is first treated so that tagged and untagged spots read as different letters. **Bisulfite** (a salt solution) turns every untagged C into a U, which reads as T; a tagged C stays C. **EM-seq** does the same with enzymes instead, and damages the DNA far less. After either, a tag shows up as a C and a missing tag as a T. **Conversion failure** is an untagged C the chemistry missed: it stays C and looks tagged. The chain measures it on every sample, from the C's outside CpG pairs, which are almost never tagged in blood and most body cells, and prints it in every report. Then the treated DNA is read, either by an **array** (millions of DNA probes that light up red or green, one pair of colors per site, so each site gives one average over all the cells in the sample) or by a **sequencer** (hundreds of millions of short pieces, each one molecule from one cell).

methods.name: Methylation arrays (Illumina 450K, EPIC v1, EPIC v2)
methods.what: One average per site (beta value) over every cell in the sample; 450,000 to 935,000 chosen sites; two-color readout
methods.industry: Most aging clocks (Horvath, GrimAge) and most cohort studies
methods.readers: Met-A, C-Score, Group-A, IAM-Atlas v2.1, IAM-Deconvolver (the commissioned readings on EPIC v1; on 450K, the atlas, the Deconvolver and Met-A for each cell read and flagged development)

methods.name: Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS)
methods.what: Every one of about 28 million CpG sites, on single molecules about 100-150 letters long
methods.industry: Reference atlases of human cell types; research
methods.readers: IAM-A, IAM-Atlas v2.1; read and flagged development: the IAM-Deconvolver and Met-A for each cell from sequencing values (with the read-count correction), the C-Score's sequencing reading, and the whole-genome IAM-A globe

methods.name: EM-seq (enzymatic conversion)
methods.what: The same readout as WGBS with gentler chemistry: longer, less damaged molecules from less DNA
methods.readers: IAM-A, IAM-Atlas v2.1; read and flagged development: the IAM-Deconvolver and Met-A for each cell from sequencing values, and the whole-genome IAM-A globe

methods.name: RRBS (reduced representation)
methods.what: A cut-and-select step keeps only CpG-dense regions (islands and promoters), about 1 to 3 million sites
methods.readers: the held error is counted on RRBS (the mouse reproduction); no IAM-A reading, because its loose share comes from the rest of the genome, which RRBS skips; the C-Score's sequencing reading failed on it

methods.name: Targeted methylation sequencing (capture panels)
methods.industry: Blood tests for cancer such as GRAIL's Galleri, which match a sample against patterns learned from people with and without cancer

methods.name: MeDIP and MRE (enrichment)
methods.what: Pull out methylated (or cut unmethylated) DNA in bulk; no reading per site or per molecule
methods.readers: none: there is nothing per molecule to count (a thermometer handed a barometer's printout)

methods.name: Nanopore and PacBio long reads
methods.what: Read the tag directly on long native molecules, no conversion chemistry
methods.readers: IAM-A: a reader is not built yet (planned)

cohort_note: **How IAM differs from cohort methods.** Aging clocks and cancer blood tests learn patterns from large groups of people and score a new sample by how closely it matches them. IAM's instruments measure a physical quantity against a floor and a ceiling set by physics. IAM-A goes further: it reads each sample against its own loose share, like checking for a fever with the back of your own hand on your own forehead instead of against a crowd's average. The C-Score reads each sample against its own spread in the same way, so a laboratory's offset cancels without any healthy cohort.

in_development.name: The IAM Sequencing Atlas
in_development.what: A second atlas, for sequenced samples only, beside IAM-Atlas v2.1 (which stays the reference for arrays). Measured, not fitted: for each of 56 healthy cell types, at every one of the 28.2 million CpGs of the hg19 numbering, it holds the donors and reads, the methylated reads, the healthy level, the spread between donors, each donor's own measured disorder, and two noise maps (sealed donor halves, and random halves of every donor's reads, which stand in where a cell has one donor). Each cell has reads at 97 to 98 % of all CpGs, about 32 times the sites an array reads, so the sequencing instruments can read a sample's disorder at every CpG against healthy disorder of its own cell type. Built from the 153 healthy sequencing inputs behind IAM-Atlas v2.1 by the one command (run_sample.py --build seq-atlas), every step checked first on constructed data with a known answer; it rebuilds from the public files in minutes. A megakaryocyte column, a large source of plasma DNA, is being added from two donors and tested on a third. Each kind of instrument reads the same biology through its own chemistry. An array reads a probe's light, which never quite reaches 0 or 1: a site no cell ever marks still reads at the array's floor, a few percent up. Sequencing counts reads, so the same site reads about 0. Healthy disorder is computed from those levels, and near the floor a small offset in level is a large offset in disorder; the offset also changes with each laboratory's chemistry and library. So each kind of instrument reads against a ruler measured with its own chemistry: arrays against IAM-Atlas v2.1, sequenced samples against the IAM Sequencing Atlas. The physics and the instruments are the same; only the ruler changes with the platform. Read against IAM-Atlas v2.1, healthy sequenced samples showed it: at the islands every healthy cell keeps unmarked they read about 14 where healthy reads 1, and Met-A followed each sample's source.
in_development.next: The healthy references every sequencing instrument reads against (Met-A, the territories, IAM-A, the coupling, the C-Score's clustering at every CpG), each with its synthetic first; then the spheres, spectra and masks at full resolution; each cell commissioned on healthy sequenced samples the atlas does not hold.

in_development.name: The information sphere
in_development.what: The second sphere. The sky sphere places a site by where it sits on the genome; the information sphere places it by how it behaves across the 79 healthy cells, so sites that act alike land together wherever they are on the DNA, and the distance between two states is the Fisher-Rao distance of information geometry, the local form of relative entropy. The sky sphere says where a change is; the information sphere says what kind of change it is. Its construction takes each site's level out first, because on real cells a site's level otherwise sets its place. The synthetic tests pass; on the real atlas it met two of three checks, and the next test reads the third against level-matched groups.
in_development.next: The test on the real atlas with level-matched lines; then a person's information sphere against their own healthy one.

in_development.name: The C-Score family
in_development.what: The C-Score reads how a change is laid out along the genome, not how large it is, against the sample's own spread, so a laboratory's offset cancels. Three versions: the commissioned one at Met-A's neutrophil sites; the whole-genome version on the globe's change map against IAM-Atlas v2.1; and IAM-A's, the clustering of held-error departures along the genome on single molecules.
in_development.next: Each version read on healthy samples first, then on tumors.

in_development.name: Every cell in a mix
in_development.what: One run of the one command finds every cell of IAM-Atlas v2.1 in a sample and reads Met-A for each, against its own healthy profile; each cell also gets its own change layer on the globe. Sites held by one cell alone are the next test, so a loss across a cell's whole pattern can be put on the right cell.
in_development.next: Each cell's healthy spread across Group-A's 278 bloods.

in_development.name: One blood draw
in_development.what: One tube, two halves: the buffy coat (the person's own white cells, long DNA) and the plasma (cell-free DNA). The one command reads both and writes one record, including what the plasma holds that the person's own white cells do not explain, and IAM-Atlas v2.1 says which tissue it came from. Constructed draws with known answers test it; a public set of matched halves from healthy people is held unread for the test that counts.
in_development.next: The smallest share each instrument reads at each depth; then the test on the held set.

in_development.name: The territories
in_development.what: Two fixed sets of sites the identity readings do not reach, each read on the A-score gauge against IAM-Atlas v2.1 at each site's own read count: the islands, sites every healthy cell type keeps unmarked, where a mark gained is disorder; and the domains, marked sites some healthy cell types hold loosely, where the hold is lost first. Every run of the one command reads both, on arrays and on sequencing, so a change outside a cell's identity sites is seen where it starts. The synthetic tests pass, and tumors read above their own normal tissue on the islands.
in_development.next: Healthy samples read Normal first, on arrays and on sequencing against the same atlas columns, sequencing samples in sequencing units as Met-A is; then tumors and blood cancers against their own healthy cells.

in_development.name: Nearest-neighbor coupling
in_development.what: Whether a molecule's held errors fall one at a time or together, read on the A-score gauge as coupling-A: the sample's coupling (neighboring CpGs that lost their mark together on held molecules, over what each molecule's own length and error count give at random) over the healthy coupling of its own cell type, so a healthy cell reads 1. The gauge's ends are counted: 0 when no two errors are ever neighbors, and the sample's own most clustered arrangement, every molecule's errors in one run. Its healthy reference comes from the 153 healthy sequencing samples behind IAM-Atlas v2.1, 56 cell types: errors cluster in every healthy cell, more in some, and read against its own cell type a healthy sample sits within 0.935 to 1.062. It asks a question from the information-theory study of methylation: is a mark kept site by site, or by a stretch of DNA as a unit? Every sequencing report draws it.
in_development.next: Healthy sorted B and T cells from two laboratories the atlas has never held, read against the band; then the first question, written before it is read: does switching off the maintenance machinery change how the errors cluster?

in_development.name: Met-A on sequencing
in_development.what: Met-A against IAM-Atlas v2.1 for a sample sequenced by whole-genome bisulfite. The atlas is built on the array scale, where a site a cell keeps unmarked reads about 0.055; sequencing counts unmarked molecules as 0. Read on the array scale, healthy sequenced cells read 0.6 to 0.8. The atlas's own build measured how the published sequencing atlas maps onto its scale (sequencing level = -0.0902 + 1.1026 x atlas level, 17 shared cells), so the chain puts each atlas column in sequencing units before comparing. The atlas stays the ruler and nothing new is fitted. Planted healthy sequencing samples read 1.00 on average, and a 5 % loss of pattern reads about 1.9.
in_development.next: Its healthy band from the 153 healthy sequencing samples behind the atlas; then healthy sorted B and T cells from two laboratories the atlas has never held, read against that band. Each instrument that meets its bar there is commissioned on sequenced B and T cells.

report._rule: The report's explanations, one per section (author: 'a thorough, professional explanation of what it measures, where it comes from, and what it compares to'; 'populated via code from the same database'). CANON/report_text.py writes them into the chain (Runtime Matrices/Report/report_text.json) for report_v4.py; never edited in the report. No result numbers here: each section's numbers come from the sample's own bundle, and each status line from the commissioning record.

intro.title: How to read this report
paragraphs: A methyl mark on DNA is a stored record. A cell writes it and then has to keep it against the constant agitation of heat, and keeping a record costs energy. Landauer's principle sets the least energy needed to hold one bit against heat; IAM's Law is that the same cost governs every physical record, from a qubit or a transistor to a methyl mark. For a cell this gives a scale that is not fitted to any group of people: a floor, where heat alone would set the error, and saturation, where a site has lost its mark entirely and reads as a coin flip. A healthy cell sits at a measured place between the two.

Every reading in this report is a ratio to its healthy expectation, so healthy reads 1. Readings are disorder in bits (Shannon entropy of the methylation level at each site), never a difference from a control group's average. Above 1 means more disorder than the healthy expectation: marks are being lost or gained where the healthy cell holds them. Below 1 means more order than expected.

The healthy expectation is built from this sample itself wherever possible: IAM-Atlas v2.1, 79 purified healthy human cell types, mixed in the shares the IAM-Deconvolver finds in this sample. No other person's sample is needed for the atlas readings, and IAM-A on sequencing needs none at all: its healthy mark is computed from the sample's own molecules.

The genome is read with the statistical methods cosmology built to map the microwave sky. Cosmologists read a faint signal spread over millions of positions, through instruments that each carry their own offset, and still state how sure they are at every point. The atlas was fitted the way a sky map is made (every source at once, each source's offset fitted beside the biology, an uncertainty at every value). Every site is placed on a HEALPix sphere, the equal-area pixelization of the Planck and WMAP maps, so clustered change shows as patches and scattered noise as speckle, and the sky's own measures (masks, power spectra, clustering) apply unchanged.

Status. Each reading carries its status. Commissioned means the instrument passed a test written and sealed before its data was seen, in the scope it was tested on. Development means the reading is produced by the same chain and shown so it can be examined, but it has not yet passed its own sealed test; it is flagged and is not to be used as a finding. This report is for research use only.

v4-shares.measures: The share of each of IAM-Atlas v2.1's 79 healthy cell types in the sample, each with its range.
v4-shares.source: The sample's own methylation levels at the sites that differ between cell types, matched against the atlas's healthy profiles; each share comes with the range the information supports.
v4-shares.compares: The atlas's healthy cell profiles. Nothing is assumed about which cells belong in a specimen: the Deconvolver reports what fits.
v4-shares.physics: A mixed sample is a weighted sum of its cells' records. Separating the mix first means every later reading compares each site with the healthy value for this person's own mix, so a shift in cell counts is never read as a change in the cells themselves.
v4-shares.significance: Most of the difference between whole-blood samples is how many of each cell they hold. Measuring the mix, with its uncertainty, turns that from a nuisance into a reading of the immune system, and protects every other reading from it.
v4-shares.status_extra: Shares of other cell types are development and are flagged as such in the table.

v4-atlas.measures: The ruler every atlas reading is set against, and whether this array was put on the atlas's scale first.
v4-atlas.source: IAM-Atlas v2.1: the healthy methylation profile of 79 purified human cell types at 813,951 sites, fitted at once from 21 public sources as one hierarchical model, so every value carries its own uncertainty. The ruler maps the array's own anchor sites (sites every healthy cell type holds unmarked, outside CpG islands and their shores, and sites every cell type holds marked) onto the atlas's values, one straight line per probe design.
v4-atlas.compares: The atlas's values at the same anchors. The shift applied is printed, never hidden.
v4-atlas.physics: Each array, chip type and laboratory reads the same biology with its own offset and compression. A standard that every array is calibrated to plays the part a frequency standard plays on a power grid: one reference, so a reading means the same thing in any laboratory.
v4-atlas.significance: With every sample on one ruler, no laboratory needs its own healthy group to read a sample. The anchors exclude the places where early change is known to concentrate, so the ruler cannot absorb the signal it is meant to reveal.
v4-atlas.sky: Map-making with a posterior: the atlas was fitted the way a microwave-sky map is, every source at once with its own offset (destriping), and an uncertainty at every value.

v4-whole.measures: Whether the sample as a whole has departed from its own expected healthy self: disorder over every atlas site, not only cell identity sites.
v4-whole.source: At each site, the entropy of the sample's methylation level against the entropy of the atlas mixed in this sample's own cell shares. Each site counts by how firmly a healthy sample of this mix holds it (its distance from a half-held level), so firmly held sites count most and half-held sites least. Nothing is selected by hand and nothing is fitted.
v4-whole.compares: The sample's own expected healthy self: IAM-Atlas v2.1 in this person's mix. It is also split by where the sites lie: cell identity sites, islands, loosely held domains, and the rest, so a change can be traced to where it comes from.
v4-whole.physics: A held mark sits near 0 or 1, where its entropy is low; a mark lost or gained moves toward 0.5, where entropy is highest (1 bit). The ratio measures how much of the order the healthy cells hold has been lost, in physical units.
v4-whole.significance: The most sensitive reading in the report: it moves when anything in the sample departs, including changes outside the cells' identity sites. Measured on healthy bloods, reading every site makes a loss easier to see in one person than reading identity sites alone. The per-cell readings below then say which cell moved.

v4-each.measures: How far each cell found in the sample has drifted from its own healthy identity, cell by cell.
v4-each.source: Each cell's identity sites: up to 6,000 sites the cell holds mostly marked or mostly unmarked, steady from one healthy sample to the next, and chosen away from the ends so that wear can show. Read against that cell's healthy profile in IAM-Atlas v2.1, inside this sample's mix. A cell is read when at least half its identity sites are measured, and flagged below the commissioned coverage.
v4-each.compares: Each cell's own healthy profile in the atlas, weighted by its share in this sample.
v4-each.physics: Identity sites are where a cell's record is most firmly held, so drift there is the cell losing hold of what it is. Entropy rises from near 0 toward 1 bit as a site drifts toward a coin flip.
v4-each.significance: When the whole-sample reading moves, these say where: which cell's identity is slipping. A rare cell needs a larger change to show, because its DNA is a smaller part of the sample.

v4-meta-c.measures: The commissioned Met-A: the neutrophil's drift from its healthy identity, in bits, on the physics gauge.
v4-meta-c.source: The neutrophil's identity sites, read against Met-A's frozen healthy reference and tared against healthy arrays read in the same run.
v4-meta-c.compares: Healthy neutrophil references, so healthy reads 1, on a gauge whose floor (the least entropy a cell can carry and still hold its identity) and saturation (every identity site fully scrambled) are derived from physics.
v4-meta-c.physics: The floor and saturation are derived, not fitted; only the healthy mark is measured. A reading is the state of the record itself, not a difference from a group's average.
v4-meta-c.significance: The reading that has passed a sealed test. Where this sample is outside its commissioned scope, the reading is still shown, and says so.

v4-territories.measures: Disorder at two fixed sets of sites the identity readings do not reach: islands every healthy cell type keeps unmarked, and marked sites some healthy cell types hold loosely (domains).
v4-territories.source: Two fixed rules on IAM-Atlas v2.1 over the sites measured in all 79 cell types; nothing chosen by hand. Each set is read against the atlas in this sample's mix, with the mean level change beside it.
v4-territories.compares: The sample's own expected healthy self at those sites.
v4-territories.physics: An island no healthy cell marks has a single healthy state, unmarked; a mark gained there is a departure no healthy cell makes. A loosely held domain is where a held mark costs the most to keep and is the first to slip. Both are read as disorder in bits, the same physics as Met-A.
v4-territories.significance: These are the two places in the genome where early methylation change is best documented, and neither falls among the cells' identity sites. Reading them per person, against physics and the atlas, adds the most sensitive known places to the report without any training on cases.

v4-cscores.measures: Whether the sample's departures are scattered along the genome or clustered in runs, asked of four maps.
v4-cscores.source: The departures in genome order, grouped in blocks of 10 neighboring sites: the variance of the block means (scaled by the square root of the block size) over the variance of single sites. Scattered departures give 1; departures that run along the genome give more. 1. Commissioned: the neutrophil's identity sites. 2. Whole genome: every atlas site. 3. Each cell: that cell's identity sites, in this sample's mix. 4. IAM-A: the held error region by region, on sequencing.
v4-cscores.compares: Its own statistic under scattered change, which is 1 by construction; the commissioned C-Score also has a healthy band set on healthy arrays from many laboratories.
v4-cscores.physics: It does not depend on how large the departures are, only on how they are laid out. Ordinary wear is local and random; a process that acts on a stretch of DNA moves neighbors together.
v4-cscores.significance: It separates ordinary aging, which wears marks here and there, from change that acts on whole stretches of the genome, and it sees small changes because it reads thousands of sites at once.
v4-cscores.sky: The question a power spectrum asks of the microwave sky (is the structure random, or does it have scale?) asked of the genome's map.
v4-cscores.status_extra: This applies to the first C-Score only; the whole-genome, each-cell and IAM-A C-Scores are development.

v4-iama.measures: On single DNA molecules, how often a held mark has been lost where its neighbors on the same molecule kept theirs (the held error).
v4-iama.source: Sequencing reads: each molecule's run of marks. The sample's own loose share (how much of its genome it holds loosely) predicts its expected held error on a line whose form comes from the physics and whose two constants were counted once on 56 healthy cell types.
v4-iama.compares: The sample itself. Its healthy mark is computed from its own molecules, so no control group enters the reading.
v4-iama.physics: Holding a mark costs energy. Across healthy cell types the energy that holds a methyl mark is the same within its spread, a fraction of one ATP per site, and the held error follows from it. The floor (heat alone) and saturation (half the sites unwritten) are derived.
v4-iama.significance: The reference is inside the sample. It needs sequencing input; arrays carry no single molecules, so on an array it says so and does not run.

v4-groupa.measures: Whether a whole group has moved from its healthy group.
v4-groupa.source: Each person read by this same command; each reading centered on healthy people run the same way; the two groups' averages compared, with the smallest difference the study could have found printed beside it.
v4-groupa.compares: A healthy group read by the identical chain.
v4-groupa.physics: One physical reading per person, each against the expected value for that person's own cell mix, with nothing fitted across sites.
v4-groupa.significance: One person's whole blood cannot show a change of about one percent; a group can. It is a series reading, reported in the series summary; on a single sample it states that.

v4-globe-sum.measures: Where on the genome the sample changed.
v4-globe-sum.source: Every site placed at a fixed place on a HEALPix sphere by its position in the genome; the sample laid over its healthy reference (the atlas in this person's mix); a block of 10 neighboring sites lit only when its mean departure crosses the line pure chance crosses less than once in 20 samples over all blocks (5 % family-wise).
v4-globe-sum.compares: The sample's own healthy reference, site for site.
v4-globe-sum.physics: Equal-area pixels, so no part of the genome is stretched; no edges or seams; neighbors share patches, so clustered change shows as patches and scattered noise as speckle.
v4-globe-sum.significance: A picture of where change sits, drawn by a rule fixed before the sample is read. A slider only fades the unchanged background; it never decides what changed.
v4-globe-sum.sky: The same sphere and pixelization the Planck and WMAP missions used to map the cosmic microwave background, so the sky's masks and measures apply unchanged.

v4-sphere.measures: Which cell programs moved, and how far the sample sits from its own expected healthy self in information geometry.
v4-sphere.source: Every site placed by how it behaves across the atlas's 79 cell types (each site's own level taken out first), so sites that work together sit together wherever they lie on the DNA. Nobody placed them: the construction is fixed and nothing is fitted. The sample is read territory by territory against its own expected healthy self.
v4-sphere.compares: The sample's own expected healthy self. Each territory is judged against the sample's other territories, so the person's unchanged programs are the control for a changed one.
v4-sphere.physics: Information is spherical in a strict sense: a site at methylation level b is the point (sqrt b, sqrt(1 - b)) on a circle of radius 1, and the distance between two states is the angle between their points, the Fisher-Rao distance, the local form of relative entropy, the quantity IAM's Law bounds.
v4-sphere.significance: The globe says where on the genome a change is; this sphere says what kind of change it is. A program failing at sites spread over many chromosomes is scattered dots on the globe but one territory here.
v4-sphere.sky: The microwave sky is a sphere because it is the surface of last scattering seen from one place; this sphere is a sphere because probabilities live on one. The same tools (masks, spectra, cross-spectra of two readings) apply to both.

v4-ceiling.measures: How close each atlas reading sits to the derived entropy ceiling, the right-hand mark of the gauge, and whether any part of the sample has passed it.
v4-ceiling.source: Arithmetic on the readings above, nothing new measured and nothing fitted. A site's entropy peaks at 1 bit when its level reaches 0.5, so a reading of the form 'disorder over its healthy expectation' can rise no higher than its saturation: every site at 1 bit, divided by the healthy expectation. Distance to the ceiling is (saturation - reading) / (saturation - 1): 1 at the healthy expectation, 0 at the ceiling.
v4-ceiling.compares: The ceiling the physics sets for this sample's own expectation. The turnover share is the share of sites whose level has crossed 0.5 to the far side of their healthy state.
v4-ceiling.physics: Past the ceiling the reading turns over: a held mark that keeps being lost moves from 0.5 toward 0 and its entropy falls again, so a badly damaged sample would read lower than its damage warrants. The derivation says a sample should not reach that point; the turnover share is the check.
v4-ceiling.significance: It answers how far from the ceiling a sample arrives, with no free parameter, and it guards every reading against the one way the gauge could under-read. It is informative near the ceiling and says little about a sample in the healthy range, which is expected to read close to 1.

coverage._rule: One source for the table of what each instrument is referenced against and which instrument covers its blind spot (author: 'those are also filling blind spots'; 'that table belongs in the instrument document'). Status is read from each instrument's commissioned field, never typed here.
coverage.intro: IAM-Atlas v2.1 comes first because nearly every other reading is made against it: it is the shared ruler, built once from healthy cells with a stated uncertainty at every site. No instrument here needs a healthy cohort from the same laboratory. Each is referenced against something it carries with it: the sample's own molecules, the atlas mixed in the person's own cells, the sample's own departures, or physics. Each also has a blind spot, and the last column names the instrument that sees what it cannot. No instrument stands alone.

rows.name: IAM-Atlas v2.1
rows.against: healthy cells from 21 published sources, arrays and sequencing, fit in one hierarchical model, with each source's own offset measured in a calibration stage and held apart from the cells
rows.derived: nothing: it is the measured ruler, with a stated uncertainty at every site
rows.measured_once: every site in each of its 79 cell types, built once and shared by every laboratory
rows.blind_to: cell types it does not hold, and sites no source measured (left blank, never filled in)
rows.covered_by: the IAM-Deconvolver's leftover and the unexpected-cell flag; a new cell type enters only through its own sealed test

rows.name: IAM-A
rows.against: the sample's own molecules: its loose share predicts the held error a healthy cell of its kind makes
rows.derived: the floor, the ceiling and the self-reference line
rows.blind_to: arrays: it needs single molecules, so a sequenced sample

rows.name: Met-A, whole sample
rows.against: IAM-Atlas v2.1 mixed in the person's own cell shares, with the array's own blur measured on the atlas's anchor sites
rows.derived: the ceiling, the read-count correction, the array's blur
rows.blind_to: a loss spread evenly over every site, the anchors included; which cell changed
rows.covered_by: Met-A for each cell, the territories, IAM-A

rows.name: Met-A, each cell
rows.against: each cell's identity sites in IAM-Atlas v2.1 (commissioned: healthy references of the same cell on the same platform)
rows.blind_to: changes outside a cell's identity sites, such as the islands and loosely held domains
rows.covered_by: Met-A for the whole sample, the territories
rows.status_also: in a mix, each cell's reading is in development

rows.name: The territories (islands and loosely held domains)
rows.against: IAM-Atlas v2.1 at sites no healthy cell type marks, and at marked sites some cell types hold loosely
rows.derived: the expectation at each site's read count
rows.measured_once: the two site sets, by fixed rules on the atlas
rows.blind_to: changes at a cell's identity sites

rows.name: C-Score, neutrophils
rows.against: the sample's own departures: how they lie along the genome, not how large they are
rows.blind_to: an even shift with no layout; cells other than neutrophils
rows.status_also: the other cells' C-Scores are in development

rows.name: C-Score, whole genome
rows.against: the same statistic at every atlas site, against the atlas in the person's own mix
rows.measured_once: its healthy limit, not set yet
rows.covered_by: the C-Score for each cell, Met-A

rows.name: C-Score, each cell
rows.against: each cell's departure map at its identity sites
rows.measured_once: its healthy limit, not set yet
rows.blind_to: a loss spread evenly through one cell

rows.name: IAM-A's C-Score (version 2)
rows.against: each region's held error predicted from that region's own loose share

rows.name: Group-A
rows.against: a group against the healthy in the same series, each reading tared on its own chip
rows.derived: the comparison, a difference in standard errors

rows.name: IAM-Deconvolver
rows.derived: nothing: it is a fit to known healthy cells
rows.blind_to: cells the atlas does not hold, which are absorbed into a share
rows.covered_by: its leftover reading and the unexpected-cell flag

rows.name: The information sphere
rows.measured_once: the layout, once, from the atlas
rows.blind_to: changes shared by the whole sample, which it scales away
rows.covered_by: its own Fisher-Rao distance, Met-A for the whole sample

rows.name: Distance to the ceiling
rows.against: the entropy ceiling physics sets for the sample's own expectation
rows.blind_to: a sample in the healthy range, where it says nothing
